refuted.why: The 5-ticker figures are roughly right for typical stocks, but the general rules drawn from them do not hold market-wide. (1) KAMA does not converge within 10-119 bars in general: on flat or noisy stocks the smoothing constant falls to (2/31)^2, about 0.0042, so a start-of-history error decays very slowly. (2) CMO is classed as finite-window ('converges at its first valid bar'), but it is not. Its n-bar sums are running sums (sum = sma x n, indicators.ts:46-56), and on non-integer split-adjusted prices a flat window can carry residue. (3) StochRSI, Supertrend and PSAR have much longer tails than the sample showed. (4) The pattern statement '100-200 typical, up to 670-760 on BEKS' is exceeded.

refuted.why: The O(N*n) classification and 'no registry maximum length' are correct: registry params have only min, except std_dev max 50 on I27/I28/I29, and registry.ts:62 enforces only p.max. The whole-market seconds, however, were extrapolated from one long-history ticker (BBCA x 845). Measured across the real market, where tickers have 74-2,127 bars and cost scales with (N-n)*n, they are 40-60% lower.

uncertain.why:
This is a PROPOSED design, not a fact, so it cannot be confirmed. Its premises held under my checks:
- Feature 04 is identical market-wide.
- Computing all 27 defaults is cheap (6.55 s for the market).
- Custom parameters must use full history. A tail is unsafe for long lengths: with only the last 1,000 bars, EMA 200 differs at the latest bar on 508/575 tickers (worst 6.2e-4 rel) and MACD 50/200/20 on 566/575 (NFCX -2.85 vs -3.18). With 500 bars, EMA 200 is up to 7.7% off and MACD flips sign. With 1,000 bars KAMA default still differs on BABP (v_tail_custom.txt, v_converge_max.txt).
Still open and approval-dependent: where the snapshot lives, and that IHSG's Feature 04 values are in Feature_04_Technical_Indicator_INDEX rather than the main table.

additional_findings:
The prototype has two indicator engines, not one (FACT).
- The auditor compared only XI (lines 866-968, the 53-indicator builder).
- The 'Technical metrics' catalog (lines 794-847) uses a second helper set (lines 753-777): EMA seeded with a[0] (line 754), MACD whose signal is an EMA over NaN->0, RSI with l||1e-9, STOCH with 50-filled warm-up, DMI, ATR as a running mean with TR on bar 0 = H-L, BB, SUPERTREND, ICHI, bullDiv.
- Every Technical preset therefore runs on this second engine: Minervini, golden, oversold, rebound, squeeze, stflip, ichi and macddiv (lines 1091-1100).
- Porting the presets means mapping price_ma, ma_cross, rsi, stoch, macd, adx, bb, atr and supertrend onto F[key].
- The EMA option of price_ma will change in warm-up (SMA seed vs a[0] seed).
- Ichimoku (the 'ichi' preset) has no indicator in the 53-key registry.
- bullDiv (line 772) uses the same pivot and divergence logic as Backtest bullishDivergence (conditions.ts:140-155), so it can be reused.

Prices are split-adjusted before 2026-09-12 and raw after (FACT).
- 150,797 price rows across 181 tickers have non-integer OHLC (query). The history is mixed: BACKTEST_END_TO_END.md section 3 'Price adjustment'; ADJUSTED_HISTORY_BOUNDARY in apps/edge-bff/backtest/src/core/engine.ts.
- This causes the running-sum residue artefacts in CMO, UO and Bollinger.
- INFERENCE: a split after 2026-09-12 would put a raw price gap into every indicator, identically in Feature 04 and the terminal code, so a screener needs a corporate-action warning.
- INFERENCE: any re-ingest of adjusted history changes past values, so a snapshot must be rebuilt for each ticker whose price changes.

Feature 04 coverage of IHSG (FACT; replaces the auditor's INFERENCE).
- IHSG has 0 rows in Feature_04_Technical_Indicator.
- It has 2,127 rows (2018-01-02..2026-10-27, the same calculation version) in Feature_04_Technical_Indicator_INDEX.
- So the 829 priced tickers vs 828 stock rows on 2026-10-27 is exactly IHSG.
- A screener that reads Feature 04 must read the _INDEX table for the index.

Stale and short histories (FACT).
- 16 tickers with 2026 prices have their last bar before 2026-10-27: ADHI 2026-08-21, PPGL 2026-09-04, IPAC 2026-09-10, INPS 2026-09-16, PTPP 2026-10-02, CSMI and XSPI 2026-10-06, IGAR and TFCO 2026-10-15, BIKE 2026-10-19, BSWD and MPRO 2026-10-20, TRUK 2026-10-21, MASB 2026-10-22, MSIN and TGKA 2026-10-26.
- Their 'latest' indicator values are stale, so the screener must align on a common as-of date or flag them.
- 8 stocks priced on 2026-10-27 have fewer than 200 bars, so SMA/EMA 200 is null for them (affects the Minervini and golden presets).

Dynamic computation from a tail of bars (FACT).
- With all I01-I27 defaults computed from only the last 500 bars, the latest-bar values equal the full-history values within 1e-6 x max on every ticker except KAMA on BABP.
- With 250 bars, ADX (5 tickers, DADA 0.074 abs), PSAR (LAJU 2.1 abs), TSI signal (DADA) and KAMA fail.
- Long custom lengths need far more than 1,000 bars (v_tail_custom.txt).
- So any 'short tail' optimisation must depend on the parameter values; full history is the only safe uniform rule.

Feature 04's equity source query has no is_final filter (FACT: features/feature04/pipeline.py:49-55), while the publisher (publisher.py:56-57) and terminal-api (store.py:12) filter is_final.
- No divergence today: all 1,330,722 rows are final, and idx-price-cron writes is_final=True (price_update.py:1084).
- INFERENCE: the two can diverge on the latest bar only if a non-final row is ever stored.

Registry inconsistency (FACT).
- I27 basis_ma_type accepts VWMA, but I28/I29 do not.
- A VWMA basis on IHSG gives 0 values (verified: all upper/basis/lower null), so the Backtest would raise INDICATOR_OUTPUT_EMPTY.
- The screener should hide VWMA for the index.

AI sandbox risk.
- FACT from INDICATOR_ALIGNMENT.md section 5: the AI sandbox follows 'TA-Lib first' (apps/market-python-sandbox/app/spec.py).
- INFERENCE: model-written code calling talib.MACD, talib.CMO, STOCHRSI fastk or talib.PPO with default matype would disagree with the screener's numbers.
- The AI_formula_reference entries should name the equal builds.

Load vs compute (FACT, measured over pgweb, not the production path): fetching the full 1.33M bars took 17.6 s in 29 batches, against 6.55 s to compute all 27 defaults for 845 tickers. This is consistent with the auditor's 'load dominates' INFERENCE.

Stale RSI on flat stocks (FACT, TA-Lib semantics): RSI holds its last value through flat stretches. An 'RSI < 30' screen can therefore match a suspended or flat stock on a value several hundred bars old. This supports a liquidity or flat-bar filter. The auditor proposed one for artefacts, but this case is not an artefact: it is the indicator's definition.
